report.summary: Checkout error telemetry is present in the authorized window, but the evidence does not establish that checkout errors are elevated versus a baseline, nor a cause. Two citable metric read slices show checkout STATUS_CODE_ERROR counts alongside STATUS_CODE_UNSET counts, and a payment STATUS_CODE_ERROR series with higher counts than checkout at each visible timestamp; the only trace view (one 3-span trace, re-served identically in two windows) shows payment/handle carrying error=true / otel.status_code=ERROR while checkout/handle has status not recorded. Within 22:15-23:20Z the checkout ERROR series cycles 6,8,10,12,14 and resets, so the visible pattern is cyclical, not a sustained ramp; no prior-day or earlier-in-window baseline was obtainable because all service-level 24h/6h aggregate queries exceeded the result-size limit, and the metric-name and label-value inventory queries failed with source errors. Per-pod error series in the same view are not additive subsets of the service-level value, so per-pod distribution and label coverage remain unresolved.

claims.text: A traces search for service=checkout over 2026-10-21T23:21:32Z-2026-10-22T23:21:32Z returned exactly one trace containing three spans: frontend/handle (5000 us, no parent reference), checkout/handle (4000 us, status_state not_recorded, parent CHILD_OF span 3093090000000000), and payment/handle (3000 us, status_state recorded with status_tags error=true and otel.status_code=ERROR, parent CHILD_OF span 3093090000000000).

A second traces search restricted to 2026-10-22T20:21:32Z-2026-10-22T23:21:32Z returned the same three spans with identical span IDs (3093090000000000, 3093090000000001, 3093090000000002), identical durations (5000/4000/3000 us) and the same payment/handle error tags, so the sampled trace view did not supply distinct traces for the two windows.

In a read slice of a checkout/payment error-aggregation result, the timestamp 1792711292.0 (= 2026-10-22T23:21:32Z) shows service-level series checkout STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 6, checkout STATUS_CODE_UNSET = 30 and payment STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 9, plus individual per-pod checkout STATUS_CODE_ERROR series with values 1 through 7.

In a read slice covering 2026-10-22T22:15Z-23:20Z at 300s step, the checkout STATUS_CODE_ERROR series takes values 6,8,10,12,14 and then repeats that sequence in each subsequent 5-point cycle, the checkout STATUS_CODE_UNSET series cycles 30,31,32,33,34, and the payment STATUS_CODE_ERROR series cycles 9,12,15,18,21.

Within the same read slice, the checkout service-level STATUS_CODE_ERROR value at timestamp 1792711200.0 is 12 while individual per-pod checkout error series at that timestamp show 13 (pod-000), 17 (pod-001) and 21 (pod-002), which cannot be additive subsets of 12; the per-pod error breakdown and label semantics are therefore not reconcilable from this view.

The only trace view available shows payment/handle's sole visible parent reference pointing to the frontend span 3093090000000000, not to the checkout span, so this sampled trace does not evidence a checkout-to-payment call edge; both checkout/handle and payment/handle appear as siblings under the frontend span.

Rejected: that the sampled traces show an increasing error trend or a failing-request count for checkout. Both trace searches returned the same single 3-span trace, and trace span counts are not unique request counts, so no rate or trend can be derived from them.

The elevated-checkout-error suspicion is consistent with a companion payment error component: payment STATUS_CODE_ERROR is higher than checkout STATUS_CODE_ERROR at every visible timestamp (9 vs 6, increasing to 21 vs 14), and the one sampled payment span is the only span marked error. This remains a correlation-level hypothesis; no checkout-to-payment dependency and no causal mechanism are evidenced.

Computed from the visible series, the checkout error share (ERROR / (ERROR + UNSET)) moves between roughly 20% (6/30) and roughly 41% (14/34) inside 22:15Z-23:20Z and then resets, suggesting a cyclical error pattern rather than a sustained incident escalation; confirming or refuting this requires a comparable baseline period, which this Run could not obtain.

Re-run the checkout error aggregation without per-pod/instance labels (or with a low topk) so the query fits the result limit; the failed attempts all returned RESULT_TOO_LARGE at 403 series with 400 pod and 400 instance values, which is what prevented any full-day baseline.

gaps: No baseline: every service-level aggregate query over 24h and over 6h windows failed with RESULT_TOO_LARGE (403 series), so prior-period checkout error ratios inside the authorized window are unknown and no elevation-versus-baseline comparison is possible.

Metric inventory unknown: get_metric_names (both attempts) and get_label_values returned status error with reason SOURCE_ERROR, so available metric names, ERROR-related series for other services, and complete label coverage are unknown rather than zero.

Read slices were truncated: a9a5799c-bf80-485c-9c33-aaf1bddeb165-t0:690d24ba-7c78-4e51-b4cd-aef761b7072b returned 10 of 403 rows and 444d1749-1db2-47ac-a542-1b92d6e2f2c1-t0:e9b3ad00-a70a-4b35-8538-36f440e62cd1 returned 6 of 403 rows, so the full per-pod series set and the remaining timestamps were not observed.

Per-pod error values do not reconcile with the service-level value in the same view (13/17/21 versus 12 at one timestamp); whether these are different label sets, partial windows or differing aggregation semantics is unresolved.

Trace coverage is one 3-span trace per search with no omitted spans; this cannot quantify checkout error rate, latency distribution or a complete call chain, and no latency trend is asserted because no comparable latency baseline was obtained.
No histogram or latency series for checkout was successfully retrieved; only three individual span durations (3000-5000 us) were observed.
next_steps: Query checkout and payment error series with a baseline period (e.g., the same clock hour on prior days) using a low-cardinality aggregation so the result fits the tool limit, then compare error ratios.
Investigate payment service error telemetry and its span parent references over a longer window to test whether payment failures align with checkout error counts, without assuming a call edge.
Clarify the semantics/aggregation of the per-pod versus service-level series for traces_span_metrics_calls_total before using pod-level values for localization.
Re-attempt metric name and label-value discovery once the metrics source returns successful responses, to establish which ERROR series exist and which are simply absent.
